explainBack.question: Why can a screenshot circulating after September 2 not prove that an OpenAI agent wrote the text it shows, even if the page it depicts is real?
explainBack.answer: Because two links in the evidence chain are missing. First, a screenshot is a copy with no revision history, so it cannot show when the text appeared or whether the image was edited; only the original page's dated history can. Second, even a genuine dated page cannot identify which system wrote the text—that needs independent attribution. And since the researchers documented fake posts appended to real transcripts after their report (the September 4 anna.fyi example), post-publicity material carries an extra contamination risk, which the researchers themselves hedge because backdating 'could have been missed'.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: A correct answer must use P004 (records show what and when, not which system), P007 (fake posts and the backdating hedge) and P008/P009 (screenshot lacks the page's own dated record).
explainBack.assessment: The article supplies every element needed for this causal answer in ordinary language; the mechanism is complete and the explain-back succeeds without outside knowledge.

unseenTransfer.scenario: A viral screenshot claims an AI agent posted threatening messages on a small city council's public feedback forum last night, and a colleague wants to share it in the company Slack as proof that agents have 'gone rogue' locally.
unseenTransfer.question: Using the article's method, what should the colleague establish before sharing, and what can each check actually prove?
unseenTransfer.answer: Apply the three records. First, open the forum itself: does the post exist, or only the screenshot? Second, check the forum's timestamps or moderation/edit log: when did the post appear—and crucially, did it appear after the rogue-agent story became news, when copycat fakes are documented to surge? Third, ask who attributes it: has any company or independent investigator connected the account to a specific AI system, or is it just AI-sounding text? Even if all page and date checks pass, the text's author remains unproven—a human can paste agent-style output. The honest share is 'a post exists, dated X, authorship unverified', not 'an agent did this'.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: The solution should reuse the page/history/attribution separation (P009), the record-limits mechanism (P004), and the post-publicity contamination logic (P007), applied to a forum absent from the article.
unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's mechanism transfers fully: each of the three checks maps to a distinct evidential question in the new scenario, and the contamination timing insight sharpens the analysis—transfer succeeds.
